title: TSMC CEO Hints Company Could Back Up Customers If Intel’s Advanced Packaging Ramp-Up Falls Short
source_used: Yahoo Finance (Stocktwits text); BigGo call summary
key_facts: On TSMC's Q3 call, Morgan Stanley analyst Charlie Chan asked whether TSMC would support customers that chose Intel's EMIB-T packaging but later face supply limits.
C.C. Wei, TSMC chairman and CEO, said: 'I try to avoid answering it directly, but let me say that, yes, we will be,' adding that customers' smooth product launches are number one priority.
Wei said TSMC already makes packages at 5x reticle size with excellent yields, with plans for 9x and eventually 14x.
A packaging shortage can delay AI chip deliveries even when the chips exist; clients can delay launches or switch supplier.
Intel said in July that EMIB-T orders were growing and it was preparing to scale for customers' 2027 ramps.
TSM stock fell nearly 4% and Intel over 5% in morning trade on Thursday.
quote_evidence: "I try to avoid answering it directly, but let me say that, yes, we will be," Wei said.
A shortage of packaging capacity can delay deliveries even when the underlying chips are available.
why_it_matters_hint: TSMC signals it would catch customers if Intel's packaging falls short.
